newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT hooks 272,552 lines in Jan-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT hooks 272,552 lines in Jan-Sept.

text.p: Czech monopoly fixed-line telephone operator SPT Telecom a.s. said on Friday it had connected 272,552 new lines in the first nine months of this year, raising the total in the country to 2.67 million.
"This is slightly in excess of the plan," SPT said in a statement. But it added that it still had 633,000 outstanding requests for lines.
SPT, which is modernising and expanding its unreliable communist-era network, plans to connect over 400,000 new lines this year and 450,000 in 1997 after 247,644 in 1995.

The density of the telephone network rose to 25.85 per 100 citizens at the end of September from 23.22 at the beginning of the year, SPT said. The percentage of stations linked to digital exchanges rose to 27.38 percent in September from 18.0 percent at the end of 1995.

A Dutch-Swiss consortium of Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV and Swiss Telecom bought a 27 percent stake in SPT last year from the Czech government under a deal which obliges the company to invest heavily in higher telephone penetration.
